summary:
This page gives two short author biographies, each next to a portrait photo.

**François Chollet** has worked with deep learning since it began gaining traction in academia in **2012**. He is the author of **Keras**, one of the most popular deep learning libraries, used in university classrooms, at companies such as Google, Netflix and Spotify, and in scientific organizations such as CERN and NASA. He co-founded the **Ndea** research lab for frontier AI systems and created the **ARC-AGI** challenge for measuring machine intelligence.

**Matthew Watson** has worked on machine learning at Google since **2018**, including on the **Gemini** model and Google's open-source deep learning ecosystem. He is a **core maintainer of Keras**, focusing on its **natural language processing** tools. He holds a master's in computer science from **Stanford**, where he researched procedural modeling techniques at the Stanford Graphics Lab.

**How to use this page:** the bios hint at where each author's expertise shows in the book. Chollet's work on Keras underpins chapters 3 and 7, and his ARC-AGI work is the basis for the discussion of intelligence, the ARC Prize and test-time adaptation in chapter 19 (PDF p.600–607 per the contents). Watson's NLP focus aligns with the text and generative chapters (14–16).

paragraphs.what_it_says: François Chollet has worked with deep learning since 2012, wrote Keras (used in classrooms, at Google, Netflix, Spotify, and at CERN and NASA), co-founded the Ndea research lab for frontier AI systems, and created the ARC-AGI challenge for measuring machine intelligence.
paragraphs.what_it_means: The book is written by the creator of the main tool it teaches, so the Keras design rationale (chapter 7's 'spectrum of workflows') comes from first-hand experience. ARC-AGI reflects his long-standing view that intelligence should be measured by the ability to adapt to novel tasks, not by skill on fixed benchmarks.
paragraphs.why_it_matters: It explains why the book closes with a substantive discussion of what intelligence is and how deep learning falls short (chapter 19), including the ARC Prize and ARC-AGI 2.

questions.question: Which challenge for measuring machine intelligence did François Chollet create?
